title: Telemetry pipeline update for KV/prefix cache v2 (schema, aggregation, backfill, cardinality guardrails)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Context
We’re rolling out KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 across runtime + gateway/control-plane attribution. This ticket covers the observability pipeline work needed to (a) ingest the new v2 event/metric payloads, (b) enforce aggregation + cardinality budgets per ADR-027, and (c) support dashboards + alerts with trustworthy time series. It also defines the backfill strategy for analytics/dashboard continuity.

Owner(s)
- Primary: Nadia Rahman (pipeline schema + aggregation)
- Support: Caleb Johnson (ingestion + data quality), Mei Lin (analytics/backfill)
- Reviewers: Logan Wright (telemetry spec), Allison Grant (observability standards), Sergio Costa (dashboards), Thomas Baird (cardinality controls)

Scope
1) Schema changes
- Add v2 cache metrics/event fields to the telemetry schema (metrics + structured event payload).
- Ensure a stable contract for dashboards: metric names/units per v2 spec, with clear rollup semantics.
- Maintain backward compatibility during rollout (dual-read / dual-write where needed).

2) Aggregation rules (dashboards-friendly)
- Define canonical rollups for:
  - cache_hit_rate (overall and by dimension)
  - hit_bytes (and/or hit_tokens if present)
  - saved_prefill_ms (estimated)
  - cacheable_prompt_ratio
- Enforce consistent numerator/denominator behavior across partial-prefill and streaming retry edge cases (see known issues page).

3) Cardinality guardrails + tests
- Implement enforcement per ADR-027:
  - allowlisted tag keys only
  - capped cardinality per tag (tenant, route, model, region, deployment_mode)
  - “overflow” handling: aggregate into an __other__ bucket or drop (explicit per metric)
  - hard block for disallowed tags (e.g., request_id) at the pipeline boundary
- Build a cardinality test harness that can be run in CI for the pipeline config + in staging against sampled traffic.

4) Backfill strategy
- Define how dashboards will look during the migration window (v1 + v2 overlap).
- Backfill/bridge metrics into the analytics dataset so trendlines do not break at the cutover date.
- Document what is not backfillable (e.g., per-request outcome classification if we didn’t store the raw events historically).

Non-goals
- Changing cache algorithms (runtime)
- Customer-facing Console polish beyond what’s required to power the dashboards + MVP recommendations feed

Proposed implementation plan
A) Schema update (pipeline)
- Add new metric names from the v2 spec into the metrics registry.
- Add support for structured cache events (if present) with strict validation:
  - reject unknown tag keys
  - reject tag values > max length
  - drop payloads missing required attribution fields once v2 is enabled for that tier/region

B) Aggregation/rollups
- Implement rollups optimized for dashboard queries:
  - request_count{cache_outcome}
  - cache_lookup_count{result}
  - cache_hit_bytes_total
  - saved_prefill_ms_total
  - cacheable_request_count
- Derive hit-rate as a query-side ratio (preferred) using consistent denominator:
  - denominator: cacheable_request_count (not total requests)
  - numerator: cache_hit_request_count (or hit+partial, with partial counted separately; align with spec)
- Ensure we keep “partial” outcome available as its own series for debugging.

C) Cardinality enforcement details
- Tag policy (summary; see ADR-027 for full detail):
  - Required tags at aggregation layer: deployment_mode, region, model_id (or model_family), route_id (or route_group), tenant_tier
  - Optional tags (sampled/aggregated only): model_version (allowed only for Dedicated/Private where versions are pinned), cluster_id (internal), hardware_sku (internal)
  - Forbidden: request_id, user_id, prompt_hash, raw prefix bytes
- Overflow behavior:
  - For route_id over budget: map to route_group=__other__ (keep tenant + model)
  - For model_version over budget: drop model_version, keep model_id
  - For tenant over budget in Hosted: keep tenant_tier only (free/pro/enterprise)

D) Backfill/bridging
- Phase 0 (pre-rollout): dashboards remain on v1; v2 ingested but not default.
- Phase 1 (dual period): dashboards show v2 by default where available; v1 fallback panels for regions not enabled.
- Phase 2 (cutover): v1 panels removed after 14 days of stable v2.
- Analytics backfill:
  - For saved_prefill_ms: do not backfill unless we can defensibly approximate from historical latency fields (likely “no”).
  - For hit-rate: provide a “bridged_hit_rate” view for 30 days that unions v1-derived and v2-derived definitions, labeled clearly in the dataset.

Acceptance criteria
- Pipeline accepts v2 telemetry payloads at expected volume with no sustained lag increase >10% during staged rollout.
- Cardinality stays within budgets (per ADR-027) in staging and during canary:
  - No dimension explosion alerts triggered for cache metrics
  - Overflow rules demonstrably engaged when synthetically exceeded
- Dashboards can compute:
  - hit-rate (cacheable denom)
  - hit-bytes
  - saved_prefill_ms
  - cacheable prompt ratio
  with drilldowns by deployment_mode/region/route/model without query timeouts.
- Backfill/bridge dataset created and validated by Mei (trendlines continuous across cutover in at least 2 key views).
- Failure-mode plan documented + linked in runbook (what happens if ingestion breaks, if tags explode, or if sampling config misbehaves).

Failure-mode plan (must-have)
- If tag explosion detected:
  - immediately enable “drop unknown tags” + overflow bucketing at ingest
  - optionally disable model_version + route_id dimensions via config toggle (keep only model_id + region + deployment_mode)
- If ingestion lag > SLO or storage pressure:
  - reduce sampling for structured events first (keep counters)
  - disable high-cost derived metrics (saved_prefill_ms) temporarily
- If runtime sends malformed payloads in a region:
  - fail open for request processing (never block inference)
  - fail closed for telemetry: reject invalid events; emit pipeline error counters; page on sustained error rate

Notes / open questions
- Confirm with SRE whether alerting should segment by route_id or route_group by default (route_id can be too spiky in Hosted).
- Confirm “partial” contribution to customer-facing hit-rate (separate vs included). Proposed: display hit_rate_strict (hit only) and hit_rate_inclusive (hit+partial) internally; customer-facing uses strict unless PM requests otherwise.
- Confirm whether we need a long-term raw-event retention path for recommendation engine debugging (Optimize). For MVP, counters + sampled events should suffice.

Rollout coordination
- Must be coordinated with:
  - ENG-4816 (gateway attribution fields)
  - ENG-4813/ENG-4814 (runtime emits v2 fields)
  - ENG-4817 (dashboards/alerts consuming rollups)
- Feature flags: see enabling guide (sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/enabling-cache-telemetry-feature-flags.json)
comments: 2025-02-06 (Logan Wright): Please ensure pipeline rejects request_id if present; we had an incident last year where a single team accidentally shipped per-request tags and we ate it in Mimir. ADR-027 calls this out but worth hard-enforcing.

2025-02-10 (Caleb Johnson): I can add an ingestion-side validator + counters for dropped cache telemetry by reason (unknown_tag_key, tag_value_too_long, missing_required_tag, cardinality_overflow). Need final allowlist from spec owner.

2025-02-12 (Mei Lin): For backfill, we can union v1/v2 into a single view in the analytics dataset, but we must label the definition used. Saved_prefill_ms is likely not backfillable without a big assumptions doc; recommend we start the chart at cutover and annotate.

2025-02-14 (Thomas Baird): Please add a synthetic cardinality stress test (100k distinct route_ids) as part of staging validation. We should prove overflow bucketing works and doesn’t crash the aggregator.

2025-02-18 (Sergio Costa): Dashboard queries will time out if we have both route_id and model_version at full fidelity in Hosted. Suggest default dashboards: route_group + model_id, with an ‘advanced’ drilldown only for Dedicated.

2025-02-21 (Allison Grant): Ensure metric names exactly match the observability standards doc; we should not ship aliases. If we need migration aliases, keep them server-side only and deprecate with a date.
